record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Classify all quadratic stochastic operators V on S^{m-1} for which there exists an integer r >= 2 such that V^r(x) = V(x) for every x in the simplex.

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Describe all QSOs which satisfy V r (x) = V (x) for any x ∈ S m−1 and some r ≥ 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{m-1} = \{x = (x_1,\dots,x_m) \in \mathbb{R}^m : x_i \geq 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i = 1\}$ denote the $(m-1)$-dimensional standard simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on $S^{m-1}$ is a map $V : S^{m-1} \to S^{m-1}$ of the form
$$(V(x))_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k = 1,\dots,m,$$
where the coefficients $P_{ij,k}$ satisfy
$$P_{ij,k} = P_{ji,k} \geq 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k} = 1 \quad \text{for all } i,j,k.$$
For an integer $r \geq 1$ let $V^r$ denote the $r$-fold iterate of $V$.

Classify (describe explicitly) all quadratic stochastic operators $V$ on $S^{m-1}$ for which there exists an integer $r \geq 2$ such that
$$V^r(x) = V(x) \qquad \text{for every } x \in S^{m-1}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a well-known list of open problems concerning quadratic stochastic operators. Search results indicate the dynamics of QSOs on the simplex remains only partially understood (with results for special subclasses such as Volterra, ℓ-Volterra, ξ(s)- and permuted QSOs), and no general classification of QSOs satisfying V^r = V is available. The status is therefore best described as open.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems on QSOs, including descriptions of QSOs with various dynamical/periodic properties.
status_evidence.claim: The classification problem is listed as an open problem in the QSO problem list.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators and Their Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey notes that asymptotic behavior of general QSOs is complicated and only special subclasses (Volterra, ℓ-Volterra, etc.) have been analyzed.
status_evidence.claim: General classification questions about periodic-type behaviour of QSOs remain unresolved.
